MINUTES
  SPECIAL MEETING
  OF THE SAN MARINO RECREATION COMMISSION
  TUESDAY, APRIL 18, 2023 AT 6:00 P.M.
  BARTH ROOM, CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Yen called the special meeting to order at 6:04 p.m. in the Barth
Room, located at 1890 Huntington Drive, San Marino, California 91108.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Yen led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Commissioner Tsai (arrived at 6:07 p.m.), Commissioner Wu,
  Vice Chairperson Solan, and Chairperson Yen

  ABSENT: Commissioner Tam

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

COMMISSIONER REPORTS

Commissioner Wu shared that he attended the All City Track and Field Meet and Great San Marino
Egg Hunt. He shared that both events were well run and he heard from several constituents that
they are happy to see and learn about other community-based events.

Chairperson Yen shared that he also attended the All City Track and Field Meet and Great San
Marino Egg Hunt. He shared that he really liked the community partners area at the Egg Hunt and
hopes that the Division will consider doing this more, as well as engaging with other non-profits and
residents.

NEW BUSINESS

1. FY 2023-24 PROPOSED BUDGET

Director Johnson and Recreation Manager Covarrubias presented the staff report.

Chairperson Yen asked why some costs are being folded into Community Services Administration.
Director Johnson responded that shared resources used by both divisions are in Community
Services Administration to avoid divvying the expenses among both divisions.

Commissioner Tsai asked what the rationale was for cancelling the after-school programs at the
various schools. Recreation Manager Covarrubias explained that the School District decided to
partner with Right At School to offer those same services, and the City Manager at the time didn’t
want the City to duplicate services and advised staff to stop after-school programs. Commissioner

APRIL 18, 2023  PAGE 2 OF 3

Tsai asked if the new programming will be for that same age group. Recreation Manager Covarrubias
responded that the new drop-in programming will be for middle school students. Commissioner
Wu asked who would be running the after-school program for teens. Director Johnson responded
that Recreation staff will run the program.

Chairperson Yen added that staff should utilize any resources available through the County, other
Commissioners, surrounding cities, or community members to develop new programs. Director
Johnson responded that the hope is to continue to cultivate relationship with other cities as
additional personnel resources get added to the team. Chairperson Yen added that community
members need to be made aware of the type of help staff need. Director Johnson explained that
there are instances where professionals with unique skillsets are required to complete certain
projects.

Commissioner Tsai inquired if the programming levels for adults are increasing given the feedback
and demand, despite the decrease in the budget. Recreation Manager Covarrubias clarified that the
budget is actually increasing, but the reason there isn’t more programming is due to the lack of
programming space that is ADA compliant. Director Johnson added that once staff better
understand the space in the new building, they will work to address the gaps in service.

Chairperson Yen inquired about collaborations with community partners. Recreation Manager
Covarrubias explained that the Division is always looking for opportunities, like Trunk or Treat, to
develop partnerships and invite them to participate or work collaboratively. Director Johnson
explained that she hopes to have purposeful meetings with partners to discuss how we can
collaborate and share resources.

Commissioner Wu asked if the increase in personnel is restoring staff to pre-pandemic levels.
Recreation Manager Covarrubias explained that the changes to personnel are a response to feedback
from the community requesting more community events and the City not offering after-school
programming, causing an overall shift in programming. Director Johnson added some historical
background about when the future of Recreation was unknown and certain full-time positions were
lost. Commissioner Wu added that he’d like to see the Recreation Division fully staffed to be able
to address issues and justify the requests for the resources it needs.

Chairperson Yen communicated his full support for the Recreation Division’s budget; he voiced his
support for the increase in the budget because the Division really creates this sense of community
that is desired by residents. He encouraged staff to consider opportunities to create events that
require less work on staff and the Youth at Work program offered by the County.
